prompt:
Location screen of a late-1980s 8-bit home video game console adventure game, authentic tile-based pixel art exactly as the console hardware could show it. The native screen is only 256 pixels wide: the whole picture is built from crisp square art pixels of one size on one regular grid (each art pixel a clearly visible square block of about 6 by 6 image pixels), as if the tiny screen were enlarged without smoothing; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no mixed pixel sizes, no gradients.

Hardware limits, drawn honestly: the background shows at most 13 colours at once, taken from the console's fixed palette of strong, slightly garish colours: black, plus four small palettes of three colours each, and every 16 by 16 pixel block may only use black plus the three colours of one of these palettes. Therefore: large flat areas of one colour, solid black outlines and black shadows, no soft shading, at most two shades per material. Use only these colours: black; deep royal blue, medium blue and light sky blue for the sky and the sea; dark violet; bright orange and pale yellow for the horizon band and the lit windows; dark grey and light grey for stone; dark brown and tan for wood; pure white and bright red for the lighthouse. The picture is assembled from repeating 8 by 8 pixel tiles: the stone blocks of the quay wall, the roof shingles, the wooden planks and the ripples of the sea repeat in regular patterns. The sky is a few flat horizontal bands (deep blue at the top with a few single-pixel stars, violet, orange at the horizon) with at most one row of checkerboard dithering between two bands; low clouds as flat shapes in one or two colours. The sea is deep blue with rows of short light-blue horizontal dashes in a regular repeating pattern, and short vertical stacks of yellow dashes below the lights. The cottage window and the lantern glass are flat pale yellow; the lighthouse lamp only as a small yellow spot without any beam or rays, no smoke from the chimney, no glow halos (light and smoke are animated separately in the game).

Side view with a fixed camera at standing eye level, like a town screen in an 8-bit adventure game. Composition (landscape image): the horizon lies at about 42% of the image height. The flat walkable top surface of the quay (stone slabs) is a wide horizontal band across the whole width from about 76% of the image height down to the bottom edge; characters will walk on it. The harbour-master's cottage stands on the left at the back edge of the quay and takes about a quarter of the image width, its door at quay level. The lighthouse stands on its rocky headland on the right, its top at about 8% of the image height. The short wooden jetty leads from the quay into the water in the middle, the two small boats are moored beside it in the middle distance. Two barrels, a stack of crates, the rope coil and the lantern on its wooden post stand along the back edge of the quay; the middle of the quay surface stays free. Few big objects with clear, readable silhouettes and simple friendly shapes. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a painting, not modern high-resolution pixel art, no 16-bit look with many shades, no lens flare, no bloom, no light rays.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Character sprite sheet for a late-1980s 8-bit home video game console adventure game, authentic hand-pixelled sprite art within the console's hardware limits. The reference image shows only the costume and the proportions of the character; drawing style, resolution and palette follow this description. Each frame is TINY: exactly 16 art pixels wide and 32 art pixels tall, enlarged without smoothing so every art pixel is a crisp, clearly visible square block of the same size on one regular grid; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no texture, no shading noise.

Hardware colour limits: the sprite is made of 8 by 16 pixel pieces, and each piece uses only three colours plus transparency. The head piece uses only black, white and dark green (cap). The body pieces use only black, bright red (scarf) and dark green (vest). The parcel and the satchel use only dark brown, orange-tan and cream. Solid black outline around the whole figure, legs and arms black-grey fur drawn in black. Big head with the cap, about 40% of the height, so the striped face reads at this tiny size: a broad white stripe from the nose over the forehead, a black stripe through the eye, a white cheek, a black nose tip at the end of a short pointed snout, one white highlight pixel in the eye. Short stubby legs. Side view facing right.

Layout: one row of 4 frames, evenly spaced with wide empty space between them, all at exactly the same scale, feet on one baseline: 1 standing still; 2 walking, front leg forward and back leg back (contact pose); 3 walking, legs together under the body (passing pose, body one pixel higher); 4 walking, the other leg forward (contact pose).

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Isolated on a fully transparent background, no ground, no shadows, no glow, no frame borders, no grid lines. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
